theme: Shared infrastructure tested against original excavation plans and dated documentary contexts
question: Do named streets and services persist through rebuilding, and can seals or tablets be joined to independently dated operational episodes?
outcome: Eighteen scoped plan quantities, one independently grid-registered descriptive pair, 29 architectural source cases, 32 frozen context assessments and 78 source-specific dating entries. The fixed six-town frame plus a declared Mohenjo-daro control yields zero fully qualified persistence episodes and zero matched documentary pairs. Selective access change and renewed services are positive observations; institutional mechanisms remain undecided.
challenge: Composite phases, incomplete common excavation windows, unknown survey accuracy, secondary deposits, conflicting provenience and intrusive dated material prevent the intended causal comparisons. Multiple source uses, objects, samples and independent episodes have different denominators.
remedy: Freeze feature inventories and separate context coding before integration; preserve exact locators, north conventions, local-only source imagery, reading sensitivity, sample-to-event relations and missing reasons. Independently check arithmetic and grid fits, recount Lothal provenance rows, preserve a post-freeze Kanmer floor lead separately, and specify controls and observations that can defeat each claim.
retry_when: Acquire complete phase-keyed common windows with internal partitions, preservation controls, independently dated repairs and original-use documentary contexts. Fresh confirmation requires a new population, a power audit and frozen scoring; another seed over exposed plans or objects does not supply it.

authors.model: GPT-6 family; exact serving variant unavailable
